newsitem.title: BOSNIA: More Bosnian Moslems evicted by Mostar Croats.
newsitem.headline: More Bosnian Moslems evicted by Mostar Croats.

text.p: Three elderly Bosnian Moslems have lost their flats in the Croat-held part of Mostar in recent days amid rising tensions in the divided town, a U.N. spokesman said on Tuesday.
The evictions were the latest in a long-running campaign by armed Croat extremists, tolerated or tacitly backed by regional Croat authorities, to purge west Mostar of all non-Croats.

A 60-year-old Moslem woman left her flat for one day and returned last Sunday to find the locks had been changed and a new name plate hung on the door, Kris Janowski, spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), said.

A 71-year-old man and his wife fled their home last week after an explosion rocked their apartment, destroying the front door, Janowski said. The couple had received repeated threats that they would be hurt if they stayed in the apartment.
"The man was threatened so many times, including death threats, that he decided to leave west Mostar (with his wife) and be evacuated," Janowski told reporters.
Local Croat police were called to the apartment after the explosion but refused to hand over their report on the incident to United Nations police monitors, a UNHCR report said.
Relief workers say gangsters who dominate west Mostar profit from the expulsions, selling stolen flats for several thousand German marks without interference from local police.
The UNHCR reported 82 people have been thrown out of their flats in west Mostar since the signing of the Bosnian peace agreement in December 1995.

The Moslem-led Bosnian government and Croat separatists fought a war in 1993-94 that devastated Mostar and left the city, 80 km (50 miles) southwest of Sarajevo, divided into Moslem and Croat sectors.
Despite more than two years of international assistance aimed at reuniting the ancient Ottoman town, Mostar remains split along ethnic lines.
